source.title: Spectral Reach: Understanding Neural Scaling as Progress into the Spectral Tail
source.authors: Konstantin Nikolaou; Jonas Scheunemann; Sven Krippendorf; S. Tovey; C. Holm

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study fits loss-versus-compute scaling curves on new, relatively small model sweeps and evaluates fixed-compute model/data trade-offs. It uses the loss-scaling measurement but does not reproduce the original large-scale experiments or test extrapolation to much larger runs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports power-law fits for training and test loss on SimpleStories and CIFAR-5M next-pixel prediction. It also plots test loss along fixed-compute curves, but reports no fitted compute-optimal allocation exponents or verified optimum. Spectral-position results concern a related mechanism rather than the loss-law versions; they are recorded under fits_no_version. Values shown only in plots are identified as figure-only.
record.test_reason: The paper's own small-scale sweeps fit power laws of training and test loss against compute. These cover Llama 2 models from 1.2M to 134M parameters on SimpleStories and from 0.1M to 12.5M on CIFAR-5M next-pixel prediction, spanning about 1e10–1e18 FLOPs. This is a new data and scale setting with a direct result on the loss power law (V1) and on an image setting (V5). The paper's main aim is a spectral mechanism, but the loss-scaling fits are its own measured results, not merely assumed.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors' central conclusion is mechanistic: larger models reach lower loss because they keep learning from weak eNTK tail modes (spectral reach), and feature learning amplifies χnet to sustain this. Power-law loss scaling is reported as the setting, for train and test loss, in which this is observed. They also say χpos tracks test loss along isocompute curves, but they report no compute-optimal allocation.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures training and test loss across model-size sweeps and fits power laws, but uses small Llama 2-style models, SimpleStories and CIFAR-5M, and a single-epoch recipe with separately tuned learning rates. It does not reproduce the original large-scale runs or validate extrapolations.
record.method_sensitivity: Training configurations, including learning rates, were selected separately by model size through preliminary grid searches. The paper also reports different datasets and task settings; it does not systematically compare fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral position χpos falls by orders of magnitude during training, and larger models reach lower values; small models plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger models keep learning from smaller-eigenvalue eNTK modes (spectral reach) after smaller models stall.

fits_no_version.finding: The size ordering of spectral position persists for CIFAR-5M ViTs under muP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral reach ordering is capacity-driven rather than driven by width-dependent feature-learning intensity.

fits_no_version.finding: χnet grows under feature learning but stays constant for frozen random-backbone probes. Pretrained-backbone probes reach lower χpos than random-backbone probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature learning reshapes representations so as to support spectral reach.

fits_no_version.finding: Along isocompute curves, χpos qualitatively tracks test loss as the data/model ratio shifts (Figure 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral position follows loss along fixed-compute model/data trade-offs.

record.problems: Main language and next-pixel experiments use small datasets/model scales and only three random initializations. Learning rates are tuned separately by model size rather than systematically varied. The loss fits cover the tested sweeps but do not test extrapolation to orders-of-magnitude-larger runs. Fixed-compute trade-offs are plotted without reported optimum values or allocation exponents. Vision-classification loss curves are not fitted to power laws. Several reported fit values and allocation curves are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant reported results omitted.

untested.parts: Separate sweeps over tokens or data size with model size not the bottleneck. Only a model-size sweep under one single-epoch recipe is fitted, against compute.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small to larger runs.
Isocompute curves are plotted, but no loss-minimising N or D per budget and no allocation exponents are reported.
Not tested: no comparison of model shapes at fixed parameter count.
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested. For ViT classification no power-law fit is given.
Not tested: fitting choices, parameter counting and schedules are not varied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 limits_scope label is removed: rows R5 and R6 cannot show the allocation law, so V3 is untested. The reader's V5 limits_scope label for ViT classification is removed: no fit is reported, and untested parts are not limits_scope. Caveats on the supports labels: the models are tiny, learning rates were tuned per model size, the fits have no irreducible-loss term, and the CIFAR-5M exponent is near zero. Fit values are read from figure annotations.

versions.untested_parts: The reported sweeps vary model size while using a fixed single-epoch training recipe; they do not independently sweep parameter count, token count, and compute while establishing that the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
No procedure fits laws on small runs and then evaluates predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.

The paper plots test loss at fixed compute budgets but does not report the minimizing parameter/token allocation, fit allocation-versus-compute exponents, or establish whether parameter and token growth rates are equal.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests image-data next-pixel prediction and CIFAR-5M classification, but not video, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer. The classification results do not report a power-law fit.
No downstream-task performance is related to pretraining loss or scale.
The paper does not systematically vary parameter counting, fitting method, data, or training schedule to test dependence of exponents or curve bending.
